from PIL import Image
import numpy as np

im = Image.open('barcode.png').convert('RGB')
a = np.asarray(im).astype(float)
H, W, _ = a.shape
col = a.mean(axis=0)  # W x 3 mean color per column
lum = col @ np.array([0.299, 0.587, 0.114])
print('size', W, H)
print('overall mean RGB', col.mean(axis=0).round(1), 'mean lum', round(lum.mean(), 1))

def hexc(c):
    return '#%02x%02x%02x' % tuple(int(round(v)) for v in c)

# --- stripe segmentation by color deltas ---
d = np.abs(np.diff(col, axis=0)).sum(axis=1)
bounds = [0] + [int(x) for x in np.where(d > 45)[0] + 1] + [W]
merged = [bounds[0]]
for x in bounds[1:]:
    if x - merged[-1] >= 3:
        merged.append(x)
if merged[-1] != W:
    merged.append(W)
stripes = []
for i in range(len(merged) - 1):
    x0, x1 = merged[i], merged[i + 1]
    c = col[x0:x1].mean(axis=0)
    l = float(c @ np.array([0.299, 0.587, 0.114]))
    stripes.append((x0, x1, c, l))
print('stripe count:', len(stripes))

print('\n-- all stripes: pos% width hex lum --')
for x0, x1, c, l in stripes:
    print(f'{100*x0/W:6.1f}% w{x1-x0:3d} {hexc(c)} L{l:5.0f}')

# --- 30-bin timeline ---
print('\n-- 30-bin timeline (hex, lum) --')
nb = 30
for i in range(nb):
    x0, x1 = int(W * i / nb), int(W * (i + 1) / nb)
    c = col[x0:x1].mean(axis=0)
    l = float(c @ np.array([0.299, 0.587, 0.114]))
    print(f'{i:2d} [{100*x0/W:4.1f}-{100*x1/W:4.1f}%] {hexc(c)} L{l:5.0f}')

# --- accents ---
r, g, b = col[:, 0], col[:, 1], col[:, 2]
reds = np.where((r > g * 1.6) & (r > b * 1.4) & (r > 30))[0]
blues = np.where((b > r * 1.35) & (b > g * 1.15) & (b > 40))[0]
greens = np.where((g > r * 1.25) & (g > b * 1.05) & (g > 35))[0]
brights = np.where(lum > 150)[0]

def runs(idx):
    out = []
    if len(idx) == 0:
        return out
    s = p = idx[0]
    for x in idx[1:]:
        if x == p + 1:
            p = x
        else:
            out.append((s, p)); s = p = x
    out.append((s, p))
    return [(f'{100*a_/W:.1f}-{100*b_/W:.1f}%', hexc(col[a_:b_+1].mean(axis=0))) for a_, b_ in out]

print('\nred runs:', runs(reds))
print('blue runs:', runs(blues))
print('green runs:', runs(greens))
print('bright(>150) runs:', runs(brights))
very_bright = np.where(lum > 220)[0]
print('very bright(>220) runs:', runs(very_bright))

# --- crops for visual inspection ---
for name, (x0, x1) in {'c1_start': (0, 250), 'c2_quarter': (250, 500),
                       'c3_mid': (500, 750), 'c4_end': (750, 1000)}.items():
    crop = im.crop((x0, 0, x1, H)).resize(((x1 - x0) * 3, H * 3), Image.NEAREST)
    crop.save(name + '.png')
print('crops saved')

"**Starboy**" is a song by the Canadian singer [the Weeknd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Weeknd "The Weeknd") featuring the French [electronic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_music "Electronic music") duo [Daft Punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daft_Punk "Daft Punk"). It was released on September 23, 2016, through [XO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XO_\(record_label\) "XO (record label)") and [Republic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records"), as the lead single from his third [studio album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studio_album "Studio album") [of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starboy_\(album\) "Starboy (album)") (2016).[\[1\]](#cite_note-1)[\[2\]](#cite_note-2) The artists wrote and produced the song with [Doc McKinney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doc_McKinney "Doc McKinney") and [Henry "Cirkut" Walter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cirkut "Cirkut"), with [Jason "DaHeala" Quenneville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DaHeala "DaHeala") receiving additional credits.[\[3\]](#cite_note-3) The song reflects themes of extravagance and celebrity life.

"Starboy" topped the charts in countries such as Canada, France, Netherlands, New Zealand and Sweden, as well as the US [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), where it became the Weeknd's third chart-topper, and Daft Punk's only chart-topper. The music video for the song was directed by frequent collaborator [Grant Singer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grant_Singer "Grant Singer"), who directed the Weeknd's previous music videos for his previous chart-toppers "[Can't Feel My Face](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't_Feel_My_Face "Can't Feel My Face")" and "[The Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hills_\(song\) "The Hills (song)")". In the music video, the Weeknd is shown trying to destroy evidence of his previous self, including his own awards from his past album, *[Beauty Behind the Madness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beauty_Behind_the_Madness "Beauty Behind the Madness")*. The video has been described as the Weeknd's attempt to murder his former personality.

On November 11, 2016, a remix produced by [Kygo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kygo "Kygo") was released, which was later included on the deluxe version of the album, released in March 2023\.

## Background and release

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Starboy_\(song\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background and release")\]

In March 2016, [the Weeknd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Weeknd "The Weeknd") hinted at an upcoming project, stating that a "chapter" was done, referring to his second studio album, *[Beauty Behind the Madness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beauty_Behind_the_Madness "Beauty Behind the Madness")* (2015). He started to record new material in May 2016, inviting Mark Guiducci of *[Vogue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vogue_\(magazine\) "Vogue (magazine)")* to [Conway Recording Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conway_Recording_Studios "Conway Recording Studios"), revealing the involvement of the same team who produced his debut mixtape, *[House of Balloons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Balloons "House of Balloons")* (2011).[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) The executive vice president for [Republic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records") revealed on July 15 that the Weeknd and the French electronic duo [Daft Punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daft_Punk "Daft Punk") were set to have a session two days from then.[\[5\]](#cite_note-Complex-5)

The Weeknd teased a collaboration with the duo in August 2016, posting an image of two robot figurines atop a speaker.[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) On September 20, the Weeknd blanked his Instagram page, after posting multiple cryptic tweets.[\[7\]](#cite_note-7) On September 21, he announced *[Starboy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starboy_\(album\) "Starboy (album)")*, his third studio album.[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) A few hours later, he released the title track, featuring Daft Punk, as the album's lead single.[\[9\]](#cite_note-9)

## Development and composition

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Starboy_\(song\)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Development and composition")\]

Before recording together, the Weeknd wanted to get closer to Daft Punk for a long time, having first met one half of the duo, [Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guy-Manuel_de_Homem-Christo "Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo"), at a Los Angeles party. He told *[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_\(magazine\) "Variety (magazine)")*'s Jem Aswad:

> I just wanted to get into the studio with them — I didn't even care if we made music, I just wanted to be friends. I met Guy-Man first, out partying in L.A., and I actually partied with him more than I worked with him. He'd would ([sic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sic "Sic")) tell me, with loud music playing over drinks, how much he liked my work.[\[10\]](#cite_note-Variety2021-10)

At a Paris recording studio, the Weeknd was presented with one of the duo's draft instrumentals, which became "[I Feel It Coming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Feel_It_Coming "I Feel It Coming")". Between takes, he repeatedly heard a drum loop, later finding out that it was the drum beat for "Starboy" on Homem-Christo's phone. The song was written in 30 minutes,[\[11\]](#cite_note-11) and was finished with "I Feel It Coming" in a span of 4 days.[\[10\]](#cite_note-Variety2021-10)

"Starboy" was written by the Weeknd, [Thomas Bangalter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Bangalter "Thomas Bangalter"), Homem-Christo, [Doc McKinney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doc_McKinney "Doc McKinney"), [Cirkut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cirkut "Cirkut"), and [DaHeala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DaHeala "DaHeala"). It was produced by Daft Punk. The track was recorded at Gang Studio in [Paris, France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris,_France "Paris, France"), and [Conway Recording Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conway_Recording_Studios "Conway Recording Studios") in Los Angeles, California, and engineered by Florian Lagatta, McKinney, Cirkut, and Josh Smith. It was mixed at MixStar Studios in [Virginia Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Beach "Virginia Beach") by [Serban Ghenea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serban_Ghenea "Serban Ghenea"), with John Hanes serving as mixing engineer. The track was mastered by [Tom Coyne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Coyne_\(music_engineer\) "Tom Coyne (music engineer)") and Aya Merrill at Sterling Sound, New York City.[\[12\]](#cite_note-12) The sheet music for "Starboy", shows a composition of [A minor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_minor "A minor") at a tempo of 94 beats per minute, while the vocals range from A4-A5.[\[13\]](#cite_note-13)

## Critical reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Starboy_\(song\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Critical reception")\]

The song received critical acclaim. Mehan Jayasuriya of *[Pitchfork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitchfork_\(website\) "Pitchfork (website)")* said that the song "glides like a sleek, high-performance car".[\[14\]](#cite_note-14) Christopher Bohlsen of *[Renowned for Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renowned_for_Sound "Renowned for Sound")* said, "Melding The Weeknd's dark [R&B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_R&B "Contemporary R&B") with Daft Punk's [nu-disco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nu-disco "Nu-disco") sound, the track elegantly rides the fine line between dance and [hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip-hop "Hip-hop"), the two genres *[Starboy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starboy_\(album\) "Starboy (album)")* oscillates between."[\[15\]](#cite_note-15) [Christopher Hooton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Hooton "Christopher Hooton") of *[The Independent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Independent "The Independent")* wrote, "A statement of intent and the record-breaking first single off the LP. There are no hi-hats to be found but instead an undulating, 80s-inspired pattern of popping drums over the smash-clap of a snare. It's [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music")\-y but with an edge to it. Driving music, a car stalking through LA, the tyres slurring over the asphalt."[\[16\]](#cite_note-16)

*[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")* ranked "Starboy" at number four on their "100 Best Pop Songs of 2016" list: "Centric pop with frayed edges has been the M.O. for The Weeknd ever since he first signed on to the *[Fifty Shades of Grey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/50_Shades_of_Grey_\(soundtrack\) "50 Shades of Grey (soundtrack)")* soundtrack, and "Starboy" proves the culmination and likely end of that formula. With Daft Punk in tow to provide sighing background vocals and occasionally drift the song's production dangerously close to out of frame, the spellbinding night-drive assumes Abel Tesfaye's new alternate identity with the confidence of a star big enough to dictate his own nicknames: Even the opening lines ("I'm tryna put you in the worst mood, ah / P1 cleaner than your church shoes, ah") barely bother setting the scene, since you remember where the movie last left off. "Starboy" might not have been titled to serve as a [Ziggy Stardust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rise_and_Fall_of_Ziggy_Stardust_and_the_Spiders_from_Mars "The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust and the Spiders from Mars") tribute, but it reflects how, like [Bowie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Bowie "David Bowie"), Tesfaye understands the importance of constant evolution in both his music and his image."[\[17\]](#cite_note-17) *[Yardbarker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yardbarker "Yardbarker")* named it as one of the best songs of 2016: "It's catchy, and The Weeknd's unique singing style matches perfectly with Daft Punk's house-music-tinged beats."[\[18\]](#cite_note-18)

## Commercial performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Starboy_\(song\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Commercial performance")\]

The song reached number one in Canada, Denmark, France, New Zealand, Norway, Mexico, Sweden, and the United States, while also going top five in various countries, including reaching number two in both Australia and Ireland and number three in Germany. The single debuted at number 40 on the [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), opening at number 22 on the [Digital Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Songs "Digital Songs") chart with 28,000 downloads with only one day of charting and at number 37 on the [Radio Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_Songs_\(chart\) "Radio Songs (chart)") chart with 36 million of audience, following its first full week of airplay. It became the Weeknd's third highest debut on the chart and Daft Punk's second top 40 entry.[\[19\]](#cite_note-19) The following week, "Starboy" jumped 37 positions to reach number three, becoming the Weeknd's fifth top 10 single and Daft Punk's second. Additionally, "Starboy" made the biggest jump into the Hot 100's top five since [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift")'s "[Bad Blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Blood_\(Taylor_Swift_song\) "Bad Blood (Taylor Swift song)")" leapt from number 53 to number one in June 2015\.[\[20\]](#cite_note-Hot_100_2-20) It sold 88,000 copies in its second week,[\[21\]](#cite_note-week_2-21) and 92,000 in its third week.[\[20\]](#cite_note-Hot_100_2-20)

After remaining in the number two spot for eight non-consecutive weeks on the *Billboard* Hot 100—behind [The Chainsmokers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Chainsmokers "The Chainsmokers")' "[Closer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Closer_\(The_Chainsmokers_song\) "Closer (The Chainsmokers song)")" for five weeks and [Rae Sremmurd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rae_Sremmurd "Rae Sremmurd")'s "[Black Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Beatles "Black Beatles")" for an additional three weeks—"Starboy" reached the top of the chart on the week of January 7, 2017, becoming The Weeknd's third and Daft Punk's first number one on the Hot 100\.[\[22\]](#cite_note-Hot_100_1-22) "Starboy" additionally topped the US [Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_R&B/Hip-Hop_Songs "Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs") chart, where it became the Weeknd's fourth number one single and Daft Punk's first.[\[21\]](#cite_note-week_2-21) On April 5, 2022, the song was certified 11× Platinum by the RIAA, denoting sales of 11 million units.[\[23\]](#cite_note-RIAA-23)

In New Zealand, the single debuted at number five, which was followed by two consecutive weeks at number 2 before moving to number one on the chart for the week of October 24, 2016\. This marks the Weeknd's second number one single, as well as Daft Punk's first number one single in the country.[\[24\]](#cite_note-New_Zealand-24) In the UK, the single entered at number 3 for the week of October 6, 2016\. The following week, it climbed up to number 2, held off by [James Arthur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Arthur "James Arthur")'s "[Say You Won't Let Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Say_You_Won't_Let_Go "Say You Won't Let Go")". The next week, it was pushed to number 3 by "[Closer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Closer_\(The_Chainsmokers_song\) "Closer (The Chainsmokers song)")" by [The Chainsmokers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Chainsmokers "The Chainsmokers") before spending four weeks at number 4\. Three weeks later, it flew from number 8 to number 3, due to the release of the album. That week, it also managed to reach a new peak of number 2 on the UK Streaming Chart (originally it had only peaked at number 3). It spent two weeks at number 3 before falling again, ultimately spending 15 consecutive weeks in the top ten.

Alongside with United States, the song was certified diamond in Brazil, Canada, France,[\[25\]](#cite_note-25) Greece and Poland, becoming his first in France and Poland, and second in Brazil, Greece and Canada.

### Background and development

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Starboy_\(song\)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Background and development")\]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c8/McLaren_P1.jpg/250px-McLaren_P1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:McLaren_P1.jpg)

The song and video feature the Weeknd's personal [McLaren P1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_P1 "McLaren P1"), which he drives at the end of the video.[\[26\]](#cite_note-BILL-26)

The music video for the song was directed by frequent collaborator [Grant Singer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grant_Singer "Grant Singer"), who directed the Weeknd's previous music videos for "[Can't Feel My Face](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't_Feel_My_Face "Can't Feel My Face")" and "[The Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hills_\(song\) "The Hills (song)")". It was released through the singer's official [Vevo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vevo "Vevo") account on September 28, 2016, on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube"), along with an accompanying poster which *[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")* described as "pulp-horror-inspired".[\[27\]](#cite_note-RS-27) The video has been described as the singer's attempt to kill his former/old persona, perhaps signaling he is reinventing himself with this new album,[\[28\]](#cite_note-28) by suffocating himself, clipping his old hairstyle, and crushing his glass-framed platinum records.[\[26\]](#cite_note-BILL-26)

Several cars owned by the Weeknd are mentioned in the song's lyrics and featured in the video, consisting of the [McLaren P1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_P1 "McLaren P1") in the first verse: "I'm trying to put you in the worst Mood ahh/ P1 cleaner than your church shoes ahh", followed by the [Lamborghini Aventador SV Roadster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamborghini_Aventador#Aventador_SuperVeloce_LP_750-4_Roadster_\(2016–2017\) "Lamborghini Aventador") which he sings in his second verse: "Pull off in that Roadster SV ahh/ Pockets overweight, getting hefty ahh," and finally a [Bentley Mulsanne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bentley_Mulsanne_\(2010\) "Bentley Mulsanne (2010)") in the same verse right after: "The competition, I don't wanna listen/ I'm in the blue Mulsanne bumping [New Edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Edition "New Edition").[\[26\]](#cite_note-BILL-26) *Billboard* approached John Paolo Canton, [McLaren Automotive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_Automotive "McLaren Automotive")'s director of public relations, in order to find out the owner of the car, as their website stated "Even the world's biggest carmaker couldn't afford product placement like this, let alone a boutique British brand".[\[26\]](#cite_note-BILL-26) Canton later confirmed that the car did belong to the Weeknd.[\[26\]](#cite_note-BILL-26)

In 3 weeks, the video had 100 million views. The video had 500 million views in 3 months. As of September 2025, the video has over 2\.6 billion views on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube"), making it among the top seventy most viewed YouTube videos.[\[29\]](#cite_note-youtube-29)

### Synopsis

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Starboy_\(song\)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Synopsis")\]

In the video, a man in a black ski mask and diamond-encrusted [cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_cross "Christian cross") is sitting across from the Weeknd, who is [zip tied](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cable_tie "Cable tie") to the chair. The figure then kills the Weeknd by [asphyxiating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asphyxia "Asphyxia") him with a [plastic bag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plastic_bag "Plastic bag"). The figure is revealed to be the *Starboy* incarnation of the Weeknd—his other self represented his *[Beauty Behind the Madness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beauty_Behind_the_Madness "Beauty Behind the Madness")* era. He then walks through a house full of awards that he's received, as well as a portrait of [Daft Punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daft_Punk "Daft Punk"), who collaborated on the song, and a [panther](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panthera "Panthera"). He comes upon a large glowing pink neon cross, which he grabs and uses to destroy various evidence and history of his older self, including numerous trophies, posters and a crystal chandelier, before setting fire to the closet, eventually destroying the entire house later.[\[30\]](#cite_note-30) Walking through the garage, he passes several luxury automobiles, deciding on a [McLaren P1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_P1 "McLaren P1") and drives off with a cat in the passenger seat, which transforms into a panther, as he rides off on [Mulholland Drive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mulholland_Drive "Mulholland Drive"). The video features product placement from clothing company [PUMA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puma_SE "Puma SE"). The house where the video was filmed has been featured in commercials for [Samsung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samsung "Samsung"), [Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft"), [Range Rover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Range_Rover "Range Rover"), and [Mercedes-Benz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz "Mercedes-Benz").[\[31\]](#cite_note-31)

### Reception and accolades

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Starboy_\(song\)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Reception and accolades")\]

Kat Bein of *[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")* commented that the music video is "equally moody".[\[32\]](#cite_note-32) A writer from *[Slate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slate_\(magazine\) "Slate (magazine)")* magazine drew comparison of the video to [Michael Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jackson "Michael Jackson")'s "[Black or White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_or_White "Black or White")" video, which he has been compared to frequently for his musical style. The bleak focus on celebrity and transformation, as well as the morphing of the cat into a black panther, were some of the aesthetics that resembles Jackson's video.[\[33\]](#cite_note-33)

The video was nominated for [Best Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Europe_Music_Award_for_Best_Video "MTV Europe Music Award for Best Video") at the [2016 MTV Europe Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_MTV_Europe_Music_Awards "2016 MTV Europe Music Awards") a day before its release, leaving many observers to wonder whether it was included based on merit or instead as a result of The Weeknd's popularity at the channel.[\[34\]](#cite_note-34)

"**Starboy**" is a song by the Canadian singer [the Weeknd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Weeknd "The Weeknd") featuring the French [electronic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_music "Electronic music") duo [Daft Punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daft_Punk "Daft Punk"). It was released on September 23, 2016, through [XO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XO_\(record_label\) "XO (record label)") and [Republic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records"), as the lead single from his third [studio album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studio_album "Studio album") [of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starboy_\(album\) "Starboy (album)") (2016).[\[1\]](#cite_note-1)[\[2\]](#cite_note-2) The artists wrote and produced the song with [Doc McKinney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doc_McKinney "Doc McKinney") and [Henry "Cirkut" Walter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cirkut "Cirkut"), with [Jason "DaHeala" Quenneville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DaHeala "DaHeala") receiving additional credits.[\[3\]](#cite_note-3) The song reflects themes of extravagance and celebrity life.

"Starboy" topped the charts in countries such as Canada, France, Netherlands, New Zealand and Sweden, as well as the US [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), where it became the Weeknd's third chart-topper, and Daft Punk's only chart-topper. The music video for the song was directed by frequent collaborator [Grant Singer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grant_Singer "Grant Singer"), who directed the Weeknd's previous music videos for his previous chart-toppers "[Can't Feel My Face](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't_Feel_My_Face "Can't Feel My Face")" and "[The Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hills_\(song\) "The Hills (song)")". In the music video, the Weeknd is shown trying to destroy evidence of his previous self, including his own awards from his past album, *[Beauty Behind the Madness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beauty_Behind_the_Madness "Beauty Behind the Madness")*. The video has been described as the Weeknd's attempt to murder his former personality.

On November 11, 2016, a remix produced by [Kygo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kygo "Kygo") was released, which was later included on the deluxe version of the album, released in March 2023\.

## Background and release

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Starboy_\(song\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background and release")\]

In March 2016, [the Weeknd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Weeknd "The Weeknd") hinted at an upcoming project, stating that a "chapter" was done, referring to his second studio album, *[Beauty Behind the Madness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beauty_Behind_the_Madness "Beauty Behind the Madness")* (2015). He started to record new material in May 2016, inviting Mark Guiducci of *[Vogue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vogue_\(magazine\) "Vogue (magazine)")* to [Conway Recording Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conway_Recording_Studios "Conway Recording Studios"), revealing the involvement of the same team who produced his debut mixtape, *[House of Balloons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Balloons "House of Balloons")* (2011).[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) The executive vice president for [Republic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records") revealed on July 15 that the Weeknd and the French electronic duo [Daft Punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daft_Punk "Daft Punk") were set to have a session two days from then.[\[5\]](#cite_note-Complex-5)

The Weeknd teased a collaboration with the duo in August 2016, posting an image of two robot figurines atop a speaker.[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) On September 20, the Weeknd blanked his Instagram page, after posting multiple cryptic tweets.[\[7\]](#cite_note-7) On September 21, he announced *[Starboy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starboy_\(album\) "Starboy (album)")*, his third studio album.[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) A few hours later, he released the title track, featuring Daft Punk, as the album's lead single.[\[9\]](#cite_note-9)

## Development and composition

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Starboy_\(song\)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Development and composition")\]

Before recording together, the Weeknd wanted to get closer to Daft Punk for a long time, having first met one half of the duo, [Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guy-Manuel_de_Homem-Christo "Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo"), at a Los Angeles party. He told *[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_\(magazine\) "Variety (magazine)")*'s Jem Aswad:

> I just wanted to get into the studio with them — I didn't even care if we made music, I just wanted to be friends. I met Guy-Man first, out partying in L.A., and I actually partied with him more than I worked with him. He'd would ([sic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sic "Sic")) tell me, with loud music playing over drinks, how much he liked my work.[\[10\]](#cite_note-Variety2021-10)

At a Paris recording studio, the Weeknd was presented with one of the duo's draft instrumentals, which became "[I Feel It Coming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Feel_It_Coming "I Feel It Coming")". Between takes, he repeatedly heard a drum loop, later finding out that it was the drum beat for "Starboy" on Homem-Christo's phone. The song was written in 30 minutes,[\[11\]](#cite_note-11) and was finished with "I Feel It Coming" in a span of 4 days.[\[10\]](#cite_note-Variety2021-10)

"Starboy" was written by the Weeknd, [Thomas Bangalter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Bangalter "Thomas Bangalter"), Homem-Christo, [Doc McKinney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doc_McKinney "Doc McKinney"), [Cirkut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cirkut "Cirkut"), and [DaHeala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DaHeala "DaHeala"). It was produced by Daft Punk. The track was recorded at Gang Studio in [Paris, France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris,_France "Paris, France"), and [Conway Recording Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conway_Recording_Studios "Conway Recording Studios") in Los Angeles, California, and engineered by Florian Lagatta, McKinney, Cirkut, and Josh Smith. It was mixed at MixStar Studios in [Virginia Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Beach "Virginia Beach") by [Serban Ghenea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serban_Ghenea "Serban Ghenea"), with John Hanes serving as mixing engineer. The track was mastered by [Tom Coyne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Coyne_\(music_engineer\) "Tom Coyne (music engineer)") and Aya Merrill at Sterling Sound, New York City.[\[12\]](#cite_note-12) The sheet music for "Starboy", shows a composition of [A minor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_minor "A minor") at a tempo of 94 beats per minute, while the vocals range from A4-A5.[\[13\]](#cite_note-13)

## Critical reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Starboy_\(song\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Critical reception")\]

The song received critical acclaim. Mehan Jayasuriya of *[Pitchfork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitchfork_\(website\) "Pitchfork (website)")* said that the song "glides like a sleek, high-performance car".[\[14\]](#cite_note-14) Christopher Bohlsen of *[Renowned for Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renowned_for_Sound "Renowned for Sound")* said, "Melding The Weeknd's dark [R&B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_R&B "Contemporary R&B") with Daft Punk's [nu-disco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nu-disco "Nu-disco") sound, the track elegantly rides the fine line between dance and [hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip-hop "Hip-hop"), the two genres *[Starboy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starboy_\(album\) "Starboy (album)")* oscillates between."[\[15\]](#cite_note-15) [Christopher Hooton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Hooton "Christopher Hooton") of *[The Independent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Independent "The Independent")* wrote, "A statement of intent and the record-breaking first single off the LP. There are no hi-hats to be found but instead an undulating, 80s-inspired pattern of popping drums over the smash-clap of a snare. It's [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music")\-y but with an edge to it. Driving music, a car stalking through LA, the tyres slurring over the asphalt."[\[16\]](#cite_note-16)

*[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")* ranked "Starboy" at number four on their "100 Best Pop Songs of 2016" list: "Centric pop with frayed edges has been the M.O. for The Weeknd ever since he first signed on to the *[Fifty Shades of Grey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/50_Shades_of_Grey_\(soundtrack\) "50 Shades of Grey (soundtrack)")* soundtrack, and "Starboy" proves the culmination and likely end of that formula. With Daft Punk in tow to provide sighing background vocals and occasionally drift the song's production dangerously close to out of frame, the spellbinding night-drive assumes Abel Tesfaye's new alternate identity with the confidence of a star big enough to dictate his own nicknames: Even the opening lines ("I'm tryna put you in the worst mood, ah / P1 cleaner than your church shoes, ah") barely bother setting the scene, since you remember where the movie last left off. "Starboy" might not have been titled to serve as a [Ziggy Stardust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rise_and_Fall_of_Ziggy_Stardust_and_the_Spiders_from_Mars "The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust and the Spiders from Mars") tribute, but it reflects how, like [Bowie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Bowie "David Bowie"), Tesfaye understands the importance of constant evolution in both his music and his image."[\[17\]](#cite_note-17) *[Yardbarker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yardbarker "Yardbarker")* named it as one of the best songs of 2016: "It's catchy, and The Weeknd's unique singing style matches perfectly with Daft Punk's house-music-tinged beats."[\[18\]](#cite_note-18)

## Commercial performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Starboy_\(song\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Commercial performance")\]

The song reached number one in Canada, Denmark, France, New Zealand, Norway, Mexico, Sweden, and the United States, while also going top five in various countries, including reaching number two in both Australia and Ireland and number three in Germany. The single debuted at number 40 on the [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), opening at number 22 on the [Digital Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Songs "Digital Songs") chart with 28,000 downloads with only one day of charting and at number 37 on the [Radio Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_Songs_\(chart\) "Radio Songs (chart)") chart with 36 million of audience, following its first full week of airplay. It became the Weeknd's third highest debut on the chart and Daft Punk's second top 40 entry.[\[19\]](#cite_note-19) The following week, "Starboy" jumped 37 positions to reach number three, becoming the Weeknd's fifth top 10 single and Daft Punk's second. Additionally, "Starboy" made the biggest jump into the Hot 100's top five since [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift")'s "[Bad Blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Blood_\(Taylor_Swift_song\) "Bad Blood (Taylor Swift song)")" leapt from number 53 to number one in June 2015\.[\[20\]](#cite_note-Hot_100_2-20) It sold 88,000 copies in its second week,[\[21\]](#cite_note-week_2-21) and 92,000 in its third week.[\[20\]](#cite_note-Hot_100_2-20)

After remaining in the number two spot for eight non-consecutive weeks on the *Billboard* Hot 100—behind [The Chainsmokers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Chainsmokers "The Chainsmokers")' "[Closer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Closer_\(The_Chainsmokers_song\) "Closer (The Chainsmokers song)")" for five weeks and [Rae Sremmurd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rae_Sremmurd "Rae Sremmurd")'s "[Black Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Beatles "Black Beatles")" for an additional three weeks—"Starboy" reached the top of the chart on the week of January 7, 2017, becoming The Weeknd's third and Daft Punk's first number one on the Hot 100\.[\[22\]](#cite_note-Hot_100_1-22) "Starboy" additionally topped the US [Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_R&B/Hip-Hop_Songs "Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs") chart, where it became the Weeknd's fourth number one single and Daft Punk's first.[\[21\]](#cite_note-week_2-21) On April 5, 2022, the song was certified 11× Platinum by the RIAA, denoting sales of 11 million units.[\[23\]](#cite_note-RIAA-23)

In New Zealand, the single debuted at number five, which was followed by two consecutive weeks at number 2 before moving to number one on the chart for the week of October 24, 2016\. This marks the Weeknd's second number one single, as well as Daft Punk's first number one single in the country.[\[24\]](#cite_note-New_Zealand-24) In the UK, the single entered at number 3 for the week of October 6, 2016\. The following week, it climbed up to number 2, held off by [James Arthur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Arthur "James Arthur")'s "[Say You Won't Let Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Say_You_Won't_Let_Go "Say You Won't Let Go")". The next week, it was pushed to number 3 by "[Closer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Closer_\(The_Chainsmokers_song\) "Closer (The Chainsmokers song)")" by [The Chainsmokers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Chainsmokers "The Chainsmokers") before spending four weeks at number 4\. Three weeks later, it flew from number 8 to number 3, due to the release of the album. That week, it also managed to reach a new peak of number 2 on the UK Streaming Chart (originally it had only peaked at number 3). It spent two weeks at number 3 before falling again, ultimately spending 15 consecutive weeks in the top ten.

Alongside with United States, the song was certified diamond in Brazil, Canada, France,[\[25\]](#cite_note-25) Greece and Poland, becoming his first in France and Poland, and second in Brazil, Greece and Canada.

### Background and development

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Starboy_\(song\)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Background and development")\]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c8/McLaren_P1.jpg/250px-McLaren_P1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:McLaren_P1.jpg)

The song and video feature the Weeknd's personal [McLaren P1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_P1 "McLaren P1"), which he drives at the end of the video.[\[26\]](#cite_note-BILL-26)

The music video for the song was directed by frequent collaborator [Grant Singer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grant_Singer "Grant Singer"), who directed the Weeknd's previous music videos for "[Can't Feel My Face](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't_Feel_My_Face "Can't Feel My Face")" and "[The Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hills_\(song\) "The Hills (song)")". It was released through the singer's official [Vevo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vevo "Vevo") account on September 28, 2016, on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube"), along with an accompanying poster which *[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")* described as "pulp-horror-inspired".[\[27\]](#cite_note-RS-27) The video has been described as the singer's attempt to kill his former/old persona, perhaps signaling he is reinventing himself with this new album,[\[28\]](#cite_note-28) by suffocating himself, clipping his old hairstyle, and crushing his glass-framed platinum records.[\[26\]](#cite_note-BILL-26)

Several cars owned by the Weeknd are mentioned in the song's lyrics and featured in the video, consisting of the [McLaren P1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_P1 "McLaren P1") in the first verse: "I'm trying to put you in the worst Mood ahh/ P1 cleaner than your church shoes ahh", followed by the [Lamborghini Aventador SV Roadster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamborghini_Aventador#Aventador_SuperVeloce_LP_750-4_Roadster_\(2016–2017\) "Lamborghini Aventador") which he sings in his second verse: "Pull off in that Roadster SV ahh/ Pockets overweight, getting hefty ahh," and finally a [Bentley Mulsanne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bentley_Mulsanne_\(2010\) "Bentley Mulsanne (2010)") in the same verse right after: "The competition, I don't wanna listen/ I'm in the blue Mulsanne bumping [New Edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Edition "New Edition").[\[26\]](#cite_note-BILL-26) *Billboard* approached John Paolo Canton, [McLaren Automotive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_Automotive "McLaren Automotive")'s director of public relations, in order to find out the owner of the car, as their website stated "Even the world's biggest carmaker couldn't afford product placement like this, let alone a boutique British brand".[\[26\]](#cite_note-BILL-26) Canton later confirmed that the car did belong to the Weeknd.[\[26\]](#cite_note-BILL-26)

In 3 weeks, the video had 100 million views. The video had 500 million views in 3 months. As of September 2025, the video has over 2\.6 billion views on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube"), making it among the top seventy most viewed YouTube videos.[\[29\]](#cite_note-youtube-29)

### Synopsis

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Starboy_\(song\)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Synopsis")\]

In the video, a man in a black ski mask and diamond-encrusted [cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_cross "Christian cross") is sitting across from the Weeknd, who is [zip tied](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cable_tie "Cable tie") to the chair. The figure then kills the Weeknd by [asphyxiating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asphyxia "Asphyxia") him with a [plastic bag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plastic_bag "Plastic bag"). The figure is revealed to be the *Starboy* incarnation of the Weeknd—his other self represented his *[Beauty Behind the Madness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beauty_Behind_the_Madness "Beauty Behind the Madness")* era. He then walks through a house full of awards that he's received, as well as a portrait of [Daft Punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daft_Punk "Daft Punk"), who collaborated on the song, and a [panther](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panthera "Panthera"). He comes upon a large glowing pink neon cross, which he grabs and uses to destroy various evidence and history of his older self, including numerous trophies, posters and a crystal chandelier, before setting fire to the closet, eventually destroying the entire house later.[\[30\]](#cite_note-30) Walking through the garage, he passes several luxury automobiles, deciding on a [McLaren P1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_P1 "McLaren P1") and drives off with a cat in the passenger seat, which transforms into a panther, as he rides off on [Mulholland Drive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mulholland_Drive "Mulholland Drive"). The video features product placement from clothing company [PUMA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puma_SE "Puma SE"). The house where the video was filmed has been featured in commercials for [Samsung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samsung "Samsung"), [Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft"), [Range Rover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Range_Rover "Range Rover"), and [Mercedes-Benz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz "Mercedes-Benz").[\[31\]](#cite_note-31)

### Reception and accolades

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Starboy_\(song\)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Reception and accolades")\]

Kat Bein of *[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")* commented that the music video is "equally moody".[\[32\]](#cite_note-32) A writer from *[Slate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slate_\(magazine\) "Slate (magazine)")* magazine drew comparison of the video to [Michael Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jackson "Michael Jackson")'s "[Black or White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_or_White "Black or White")" video, which he has been compared to frequently for his musical style. The bleak focus on celebrity and transformation, as well as the morphing of the cat into a black panther, were some of the aesthetics that resembles Jackson's video.[\[33\]](#cite_note-33)

The video was nominated for [Best Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Europe_Music_Award_for_Best_Video "MTV Europe Music Award for Best Video") at the [2016 MTV Europe Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_MTV_Europe_Music_Awards "2016 MTV Europe Music Awards") a day before its release, leaving many observers to wonder whether it was included based on merit or instead as a result of The Weeknd's popularity at the channel.[\[34\]](#cite_note-34)

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Starboy_\(song\)&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Live performances")\]

The Weeknd performed "Starboy" for the first time on the season 42 premiere of *[Saturday Night Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturday_Night_Live "Saturday Night Live")*, along with "[False Alarm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/False_Alarm_\(The_Weeknd_song\) "False Alarm (The Weeknd song)")" on October 1, 2016\.[\[35\]](#cite_note-35) He performed the song again on *[The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tonight_Show_Starring_Jimmy_Fallon "The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon")* as a medley with "I Feel It Coming" on November 24, 2016\.[\[36\]](#cite_note-36) Elements of "Starboy" were incorporated in the Weeknd's [59th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/59th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "59th Annual Grammy Awards") performance with Daft Punk.[\[37\]](#cite_note-37) An altered version was performed at the [Super Bowl LV Halftime Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LV_halftime_show "Super Bowl LV halftime show") on February 7, 2021\.[\[38\]](#cite_note-38)

"**Attention**"[\[a\]](#cite_note-1) is a song recorded and produced by the American singer-songwriter [Charlie Puth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie_Puth "Charlie Puth") for his second studio album *[Voicenotes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voicenotes "Voicenotes")* (2018). It was written by Puth and [Jacob Kasher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacob_Kasher_Hindlin "Jacob Kasher Hindlin"). A midtempo [pop rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_rock "Pop rock") track with elements of [1980s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980s_in_music "1980s in music") soft-[soul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_music "Soul music") and [funk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Funk "Funk") music, the song finds Puth singing about how he realizes his partner was "just want\[ing\] attention" from him instead of loving him. It was released digitally through [Artist Partner Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artist_Partner_Group "Artist Partner Group") and [Atlantic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Records "Atlantic Records") on April 21, 2017, and later serviced to the radio on May 2, serving as the album's [lead single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lead_single "Lead single").[\[1\]](#cite_note-2) An accompanying music video was released on April 24, 2017, featuring Puth brooding at the club while scoping out his former partner, later returning home and finding the partner again at his apartment.

Upon its release, "Attention" received generally positive reviews from music critics for its "slick" and "groove-injected" production, further applauding the track as a more refined, mature and polished musical representation for Puth, compared to his previous releases. Commercially, the song was an international success and became Puth's signature song, reaching the top-ten in over twenty countries, including Australia, Belgium, Canada, Croatia, France, Germany, Hungary, Italy, Lebanon, Malaysia, New Zealand, the Philippines, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, South Korea, Spain, Switzerland, the United Kingdom, and the United States, where it peaked at number 5 for three non-consecutive weeks. By this, the song became his highest and longest charting entry as a solo artist on the [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") chart to date, as well as his third single to receive a [6× Platinum certification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RIAA_certification "RIAA certification") from the [Recording Industry Association of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") (RIAA), for achieving over six million certified units in the States.

To promote the song, Puth had his first live performance for "Attention" on *[The Voice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Voice_\(American_season_12\) "The Voice (American season 12)")* on May 10, 2017, followed by performances on several shows, such as *[The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tonight_Show_Starring_Jimmy_Fallon "The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon"), [The Ellen DeGeneres Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ellen_DeGeneres_Show "The Ellen DeGeneres Show"),* and *[The Late Late Show with James Corden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Late_Late_Show_with_James_Corden "The Late Late Show with James Corden").* He later performed the song on his third headlining concert tour, titled [Voicenotes Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voicenotes_Tour "Voicenotes Tour"), throughout 2018\.

## Background and release

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Attention_\(Charlie_Puth_song\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background and release")\]

The original idea of "Attention" began to develop in 2016 when Puth started to record bits of the song while he was on tour in Japan, by leaving a voicemail of the melody.[\[2\]](#cite_note-3)[\[3\]](#cite_note-4) Puth premiered the song in an "immersive music exhibit" in Los Angeles called "The Attention Room" on April 19\.[\[4\]](#cite_note-5) The pop-up installation features an LED "infinity tunnel" and is designed to replicate the brain's reaction to receiving attention. Two days later, "Attention" was officially released as the lead single of Puth's second studio album.[\[5\]](#cite_note-Billboard-6)

## Composition

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Attention_\(Charlie_Puth_song\)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Composition")\]

"Attention" is a midtempo [pop rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_rock "Pop rock") song[\[6\]](#cite_note-7) that features elements of ['80s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980s_in_music "1980s in music") soft-[soul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_music "Soul music") and [funk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Funk "Funk").[\[7\]](#cite_note-8) He also utilized the technique of [Anti-Drop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drop_\(music\) "Drop (music)"), where the chorus is minimalistic and hollow.[\[8\]](#cite_note-9) Throughout the song, the singer realizes that his partner only wants to be around him for attention and other ulterior motives instead of loving him for who he is.[\[9\]](#cite_note-10) It is performed in the key of [E♭ minor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E-flat_minor "E-flat minor") with a [tempo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tempo "Tempo") of 100 beats per minute. Puth's vocal span from B♭3 to C♭5.[\[10\]](#cite_note-11)

## Critical reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Attention_\(Charlie_Puth_song\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Critical reception")\]

Writing for *[Idolator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idolator_\(website\) "Idolator (website)")*, Mike Wass suggested that "Attention" is a "Song of Summer contender". He added that Charlie "is still the boy next door, just a little more jaded and a lot more willing to speak his mind." Praising the song's production, he said that "That boldness also comes through on the production, which Charlie handled himself, chugging along with chunky bass and faint traces of disco."[\[11\]](#cite_note-12) Lars Brandle of *[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")* described it as "polished" and "groove-injected."[\[5\]](#cite_note-Billboard-6)

## Music video

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Attention_\(Charlie_Puth_song\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Music video")\]

The official music video was released on April 24, 2017, on YouTube. It was filmed in Hollywood Hills and directed by [Emil Nava](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emil_Nava "Emil Nava"). Cameras capture Puth brooding at the club while scoping out a blond girl, played by [Samara Weaving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samara_Weaving "Samara Weaving").[\[12\]](#cite_note-instagram.com-13)[\[13\]](#cite_note-14) Throughout the song, he realizes that she only wants to be around him for attention and other ulterior motives instead of loving him for who he is. The music video has over 1\.8 billion views on YouTube as of August 2026\.[\[14\]](#cite_note-15)

## Promotion

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Attention_\(Charlie_Puth_song\)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Promotion")\]

The song has been used on its first day of release in a popular Snapchat filter.[\[12\]](#cite_note-instagram.com-13) Puth performed "Attention" live for the first time on *[The Voice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Voice_\(American_season_12\) "The Voice (American season 12)")* on May 10, 2017\.[\[15\]](#cite_note-16) He also performed it on *[The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tonight_Show_Starring_Jimmy_Fallon "The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon")* on May 18, 2017\.[\[16\]](#cite_note-17) He later performed the song on *[The Ellen DeGeneres Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ellen_DeGeneres_Show "The Ellen DeGeneres Show")* on the October 10, 2017 episode,[\[17\]](#cite_note-18) then on *[The Late Late Show with James Corden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Late_Late_Show_with_James_Corden "The Late Late Show with James Corden")* on October 11, 2017\.[\[18\]](#cite_note-19)

## Chart performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Attention_\(Charlie_Puth_song\)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Chart performance")\]

"Attention" has peaked at number 5 on the [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), making it Puth's third top ten single, his highest-charting as a lead artist, and his first top 5 hit on the chart since "[See You Again](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/See_You_Again "See You Again")".[\[19\]](#cite_note-20) He also led the Radio Songs all-format airplay chart for four weeks.

On [*Billboard's* Dance/Mix Show Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance/Mix_Show_Airplay "Dance/Mix Show Airplay"), "Attention" gave Puth his first number 1 on this chart as a solo artist in its September 2, 2017 issue, eclipsing "See You Again," which peaked at number 3 on this chart in 2015\.[\[20\]](#cite_note-21)[\[21\]](#cite_note-22)

"**Attention**"[\[a\]](#cite_note-1) is a song recorded and produced by the American singer-songwriter [Charlie Puth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie_Puth "Charlie Puth") for his second studio album *[Voicenotes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voicenotes "Voicenotes")* (2018). It was written by Puth and [Jacob Kasher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacob_Kasher_Hindlin "Jacob Kasher Hindlin"). A midtempo [pop rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_rock "Pop rock") track with elements of [1980s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980s_in_music "1980s in music") soft-[soul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_music "Soul music") and [funk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Funk "Funk") music, the song finds Puth singing about how he realizes his partner was "just want\[ing\] attention" from him instead of loving him. It was released digitally through [Artist Partner Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artist_Partner_Group "Artist Partner Group") and [Atlantic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Records "Atlantic Records") on April 21, 2017, and later serviced to the radio on May 2, serving as the album's [lead single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lead_single "Lead single").[\[1\]](#cite_note-2) An accompanying music video was released on April 24, 2017, featuring Puth brooding at the club while scoping out his former partner, later returning home and finding the partner again at his apartment.

Upon its release, "Attention" received generally positive reviews from music critics for its "slick" and "groove-injected" production, further applauding the track as a more refined, mature and polished musical representation for Puth, compared to his previous releases. Commercially, the song was an international success and became Puth's signature song, reaching the top-ten in over twenty countries, including Australia, Belgium, Canada, Croatia, France, Germany, Hungary, Italy, Lebanon, Malaysia, New Zealand, the Philippines, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, South Korea, Spain, Switzerland, the United Kingdom, and the United States, where it peaked at number 5 for three non-consecutive weeks. By this, the song became his highest and longest charting entry as a solo artist on the [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") chart to date, as well as his third single to receive a [6× Platinum certification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RIAA_certification "RIAA certification") from the [Recording Industry Association of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") (RIAA), for achieving over six million certified units in the States.

To promote the song, Puth had his first live performance for "Attention" on *[The Voice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Voice_\(American_season_12\) "The Voice (American season 12)")* on May 10, 2017, followed by performances on several shows, such as *[The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tonight_Show_Starring_Jimmy_Fallon "The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon"), [The Ellen DeGeneres Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ellen_DeGeneres_Show "The Ellen DeGeneres Show"),* and *[The Late Late Show with James Corden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Late_Late_Show_with_James_Corden "The Late Late Show with James Corden").* He later performed the song on his third headlining concert tour, titled [Voicenotes Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voicenotes_Tour "Voicenotes Tour"), throughout 2018\.

## Background and release

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Attention_\(Charlie_Puth_song\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background and release")\]

The original idea of "Attention" began to develop in 2016 when Puth started to record bits of the song while he was on tour in Japan, by leaving a voicemail of the melody.[\[2\]](#cite_note-3)[\[3\]](#cite_note-4) Puth premiered the song in an "immersive music exhibit" in Los Angeles called "The Attention Room" on April 19\.[\[4\]](#cite_note-5) The pop-up installation features an LED "infinity tunnel" and is designed to replicate the brain's reaction to receiving attention. Two days later, "Attention" was officially released as the lead single of Puth's second studio album.[\[5\]](#cite_note-Billboard-6)

## Composition

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Attention_\(Charlie_Puth_song\)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Composition")\]

"Attention" is a midtempo [pop rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_rock "Pop rock") song[\[6\]](#cite_note-7) that features elements of ['80s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980s_in_music "1980s in music") soft-[soul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_music "Soul music") and [funk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Funk "Funk").[\[7\]](#cite_note-8) He also utilized the technique of [Anti-Drop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drop_\(music\) "Drop (music)"), where the chorus is minimalistic and hollow.[\[8\]](#cite_note-9) Throughout the song, the singer realizes that his partner only wants to be around him for attention and other ulterior motives instead of loving him for who he is.[\[9\]](#cite_note-10) It is performed in the key of [E♭ minor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E-flat_minor "E-flat minor") with a [tempo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tempo "Tempo") of 100 beats per minute. Puth's vocal span from B♭3 to C♭5.[\[10\]](#cite_note-11)

## Critical reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Attention_\(Charlie_Puth_song\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Critical reception")\]

Writing for *[Idolator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idolator_\(website\) "Idolator (website)")*, Mike Wass suggested that "Attention" is a "Song of Summer contender". He added that Charlie "is still the boy next door, just a little more jaded and a lot more willing to speak his mind." Praising the song's production, he said that "That boldness also comes through on the production, which Charlie handled himself, chugging along with chunky bass and faint traces of disco."[\[11\]](#cite_note-12) Lars Brandle of *[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")* described it as "polished" and "groove-injected."[\[5\]](#cite_note-Billboard-6)

## Music video

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Attention_\(Charlie_Puth_song\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Music video")\]

The official music video was released on April 24, 2017, on YouTube. It was filmed in Hollywood Hills and directed by [Emil Nava](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emil_Nava "Emil Nava"). Cameras capture Puth brooding at the club while scoping out a blond girl, played by [Samara Weaving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samara_Weaving "Samara Weaving").[\[12\]](#cite_note-instagram.com-13)[\[13\]](#cite_note-14) Throughout the song, he realizes that she only wants to be around him for attention and other ulterior motives instead of loving him for who he is. The music video has over 1\.8 billion views on YouTube as of August 2026\.[\[14\]](#cite_note-15)

## Promotion

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Attention_\(Charlie_Puth_song\)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Promotion")\]

The song has been used on its first day of release in a popular Snapchat filter.[\[12\]](#cite_note-instagram.com-13) Puth performed "Attention" live for the first time on *[The Voice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Voice_\(American_season_12\) "The Voice (American season 12)")* on May 10, 2017\.[\[15\]](#cite_note-16) He also performed it on *[The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tonight_Show_Starring_Jimmy_Fallon "The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon")* on May 18, 2017\.[\[16\]](#cite_note-17) He later performed the song on *[The Ellen DeGeneres Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ellen_DeGeneres_Show "The Ellen DeGeneres Show")* on the October 10, 2017 episode,[\[17\]](#cite_note-18) then on *[The Late Late Show with James Corden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Late_Late_Show_with_James_Corden "The Late Late Show with James Corden")* on October 11, 2017\.[\[18\]](#cite_note-19)

## Chart performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Attention_\(Charlie_Puth_song\)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Chart performance")\]

"Attention" has peaked at number 5 on the [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), making it Puth's third top ten single, his highest-charting as a lead artist, and his first top 5 hit on the chart since "[See You Again](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/See_You_Again "See You Again")".[\[19\]](#cite_note-20) He also led the Radio Songs all-format airplay chart for four weeks.

On [*Billboard's* Dance/Mix Show Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance/Mix_Show_Airplay "Dance/Mix Show Airplay"), "Attention" gave Puth his first number 1 on this chart as a solo artist in its September 2, 2017 issue, eclipsing "See You Again," which peaked at number 3 on this chart in 2015\.[\[20\]](#cite_note-21)[\[21\]](#cite_note-22)

# Charlie Puth Is Back With A Bang In His New Music Video For "Attention"

[Kathryn Lindsay](/en-us/author/kathryn-lindsay)

[April 25, 2017, 7:25 PM](/en-us/archives/2017/04/25)

Photo: John Salangsang/Variety/REX/Shutterstock.

Charlie Puth released his new single, "Attention," just five days ago, and now the singer has [already dropped a music video](http://www.billboard.com/articles/columns/pop/7768231/charlie-puth-attention-video). The song is our first glimpse of what's to come in Puth's sophomore album, which will have a hard time [following his debut, *Nine Track Mind*](https://www.refinery29.com/en-us/2016/10/127350/charlie-puth-cancels-tour-dont-talk-health-reasons).

While the lyrics alone in "Attention" are pretty biting ("You just want attention, you don't want my heart/Maybe you just hate the thought of me with someone new"), the video solidifies their meaning. It takes place at a club, where Puth navigates the dance floor, dodging the intermittent [appearances of his ex-girlfriend](https://www.refinery29.com/en-us/2016/12/133904/charlie-puth-bella-thorne-split-tyler-posey-apology). This escalates into full-on warfare, with the duo throwing glass in a hotel room. They kiss, make-up, and then it starts all over. It's a pretty relatable story for anyone who has found themselves stuck in a toxic relationship.

Advertisement

"What are you doin' huh?" the song continues. "(You're just making sure I'm never gettin' over you)."

While we didn't explicitly know the music video was coming, Puth did tease something a few days after the single's release.

> One more thing .... ?

> — Charlie Puth (@charlieputh) [April 24, 2017](https://twitter.com/charlieputh/status/856347921003929600)

"One more thing..." he tweeted on the 23rd of April.

After the video dropped last night, the singer continued to update Twitter on its progress.

> That was the fastest I've ever hit 1 million hits. Wow ? thank you

> — Charlie Puth (@charlieputh) [April 25, 2017](https://twitter.com/charlieputh/status/856718530883887104)

"That was the fastest I've ever hit 1 million hits," he wrote. "Wow...thank you."

He later added, "3 million views in a day!!"

> 3 million views in a day!!

> — Charlie Puth (@charlieputh) [April 25, 2017](https://twitter.com/charlieputh/status/856907953474895872)

At the end of the music video, the creators added a fun tidbit: the voice recording Puth made when he first thought of the song.

"The audio you are currently listening to is the original idea for 'Attention,'" the caption reads. "While on tour in Tokyo, Japan, Charlie came up with the concept. So he pulled out his phone and recorded this voice note."

The note is just a short audio clip of the singer humming what would become the melody of the single, repeating the main word, "attention." We're not sure [*what* dramatic thing happened](https://www.refinery29.com/en-us/2016/12/132105/charlie-puth-bella-thorne-twitter-messages) in Tokyo that made Puth start writing this song ASAP, but we're glad the outcome is so catchy. Watch below!
